full_judgment: 2. The predecessor of the opposite parties No. 1 to 3, as plaintiff instituted the Title Suit No. 206 of 1974 in the Second Court of Munsiff, Dhaka, which subsequently being transferred to the Court of Munsiff, Gazipur was re-numbered as Title Suit No. 620 of 1981, against the petitioners and others as defendants, praying for establishment of title and recovery of Khas possession of the disputed property on the allegations, inter alia, that the suit land along with other lands originally belonged to one Raj Bihari Ghose, who died leaving 8 sons, and as per amicable partition made by them the suit land fell into the share of 5 brothers namely, Paresh Chandra, Jogesh Chandra, Ramesh Chandra, Urnesh Chandra and Gonesh Chandra; and that while the aforesaid 5 brothers were in possession of the same transferred the disputed land along with other lands to the plaintiff; that since purchase the plaintiffs had been possessing the same on payment of rent and mutated his name, and that SA and RS record were prepared in his name; that the defendant No.2 with an ill motive illegally and collusively by misleading the Enemy Property Authority took lease of the disputed property on 6-7-1970 in Enemy Property Case No. 60 of 1970; that the Enemy Property Authority has got no legal authority to lease out the said land in favour of the defendant No.2, as because the plaintiff is the sole owner of the land in question; and that on the basis of so-called lease the defendant No.2 forcibly dispossessed the plaintiff from the suit land which created a cloud over the title and possession of the land in suit.
